visual_action: A superimposed cutout of a young man (actor Finn Wolfhard as Mike Wheeler from Stranger Things) stands in front of a still image of Donald Trump, looking around. The scene cuts to the same young man standing in front of a still image of Joe Biden, smiling and giving a thumbs up.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: An image of him is shown on screen, and the on-screen text refers to him as "the last guy".

cast.name: Joe Biden
cast.evidence: An image of him is shown on screen, and the on-screen text identifies him as "President Biden".

on_screen_text.text: Four years of the last guy talking about infrastructure week😬
President Biden delivering an infrastructure decade with historic investment🥰

spoken_summary: There is no spoken dialogue in the video, only music.
audio_music: An upbeat, fast-paced, high-pitched electronic music track plays throughout. It sounds like a sped-up remix of a pop song, commonly used in TikTok meme formats.
editing_pacing: A simple slideshow format with one cut between two still images. A character is digitally superimposed onto both backgrounds.
manipulation_or_satire: A video of actor Finn Wolfhard (as his character Mike Wheeler from Stranger Things) is digitally superimposed over still images of Donald Trump and Joe Biden to create a meme format.
cultural_references: The video uses a meme format featuring actor Finn Wolfhard as his character Mike Wheeler from the Netflix show 'Stranger Things' reacting to different scenarios.
central_claim: President Biden has successfully delivered on infrastructure investment, unlike Donald Trump who only talked about it.
intended_effect: To persuade viewers that the Biden administration is more effective than the Trump administration on infrastructure, while mocking Trump's presidency.
